name: intraday_rsi_divergence_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when institutional algo selling (or buying) drives the index to a new 1-minute price extreme, but RSI at that extreme is higher (for a lower low) or lower (for a higher high) than it was at the prior extreme 1 minute earlier, it signals that the directional order flow is decelerating — fewer contracts are absorbing per tick even as price extends. At 5-second resolution this deceleration is visible before the full reversal, giving a 30-90 second lead. Market-maker delta-hedging amplifies the initial snap-back because they are unwinding hedges placed during the directional leg as flow exhausts. The divergence must form in RSI oversold (<45) or overbought (>55) territory to confirm the exhaustion context rather than catching mid-range noise.

indicators.name: rsi_18
indicators.purpose: RSI over 90 seconds (18 × 5s). NOT 12x-scaled from original RSI(9) on 1-min — that would give RSI(108) = 9-minute RSI, far too slow for 30-90s holds. We use 18 bars because we need the RSI to be responsive to 1-2 minute micro-moves on NIFTY. A 90-second RSI captures whether momentum was genuinely decelerating at the recent extreme versus the prior extreme.

indicators.name: low_recent_12
indicators.purpose: Lowest close in the most recent 1 minute (12 × 5s). This is the 'recent swing low' window. Compressed from the original's 20-bar (20 min) swing window because we're trading micro-divergences at 30-90s resolution, not the 5-30 minute swings in the original.

indicators.name: low_prior_12
indicators.formula: min(close[-24:-12], 12 bars rolling from 24 to 12 bars ago)
indicators.purpose: Lowest close in the prior 1-minute window (bars 12-24 ago). Provides the 'prior swing low' reference. Together with low_recent_12, implements a simplified two-window divergence detector at 5s scale.

indicators.name: high_recent_12
indicators.purpose: Highest close in the most recent 1 minute — used for bearish divergence detection.

indicators.name: high_prior_12
indicators.formula: max(close[-24:-12], 12 bars rolling from 24 to 12 bars ago)
indicators.purpose: Highest close in the prior 1-minute window — prior swing high reference for bearish divergence.

indicators.name: rsi_12ago
indicators.purpose: RSI value 12 bars (1 minute) ago — used to compare momentum at the recent swing vs the prior swing. If price made a new low but RSI is now higher than it was 12 bars ago, that is the bullish divergence condition.

conditions: low_recent_12 < low_prior_12 (price lower low in last 1 min vs prior 1 min)
rsi_18 > rsi_12ago + rsi_div_threshold (RSI higher at new low = bullish divergence)
rsi_18 < 45 (momentum in oversold territory, confirming exhaustion context)
close > low_recent_12 (price bouncing off the new low, not still falling)
buy_ce.confirmation: All four conditions met on the same 5-second bar

conditions: high_recent_12 > high_prior_12 (price higher high in last 1 min vs prior 1 min)
rsi_18 < rsi_12ago - rsi_div_threshold (RSI lower at new high = bearish divergence)
rsi_18 > 55 (momentum in overbought territory, confirming exhaustion context)
close < high_recent_12 (price retreating from the new high, not still rising)
buy_pe.confirmation: All four conditions met on the same 5-second bar

exit.stop_rationale: 3 option pts = ~6 NIFTY spot pts at delta 0.5. If NIFTY moves 6 spot pts against us within 30 seconds of a divergence signal, the thesis is invalidated — the directional flow is still strong, not exhausted. This matches the 2-5 pt typical NIFTY 30s option move range; a 3-pt stop gives the trade time to work without too much room for a false divergence to cause large losses.
exit.target_rationale: 5 option pts = ~10 NIFTY spot pts at delta 0.5. RSI divergence on NIFTY micro-moves typically precedes a 10-20 spot point snap-back as the exhausted flow reverses and delta-hedging activity reinforces it. 5 pts captures the lower half of that expected reversal at a 1:1.67 risk-reward ratio.

filters.vix_filter: none — divergence is regime-agnostic; RSI threshold implicitly filters chop
filters.time_filter: 09:20-15:25 IST; skip first 5 minutes (09:15-09:20) to avoid pre-open noise
filters.volume_filter: none — index volume is noisy at 5s; RSI level acts as quality filter
filters.trend_filter: none — divergence is counter-trend by design
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution at candle close

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — RSI divergence is classic and well-known, but systematic detection at 5s on index is uncommon; competition is primarily from human discretionary traders on longer timeframes

adaptation_notes: Original strategy traded the top 40 FnO stocks on 1-minute bars with explicit swing-point tracking over 20-40 minute windows. Converted to NIFTY index at 5s by: (1) compressing swing detection from 20-minute rolling windows to 1-minute rolling windows (12-bar recent + 12-bar prior) since we hold 30-90s not 5-30 min; (2) replacing RSI(9 × 1min = 9 min) with RSI(18 × 5s = 90s) to match the compressed detection window — NOT a 12x scale which would give a uselessly slow 9-minute RSI; (3) dropping the exact swing-low-price detection (ATR-based in original) in favor of rolling window min/max which is more robust at 5s noise levels; (4) using rsi_div_threshold as a tunable parameter instead of fixed RSI level comparison; (5) removing ATR-based stops since option premium points are used directly.
weaknesses: 1-minute swing windows at 5s bars may produce many false divergences in fast-trending NIFTY sessions
RSI(18) at 5s is still noisy — thin divergence (rsi_18 barely above rsi_12ago) may not have edge
Counter-trend strategy will suffer during strong sustained directional moves on NIFTY
18-bar time stop (90s) may cut winners short if reversal is slow to develop
